claims.evidence: The witness describes a 'slim, two-tier rectangular design', which identifies the console as a PS4 Slim, not the original 'big' (fat) model.
The witness report explicitly states that no controllers were shown.
The witness report does not mention any games being present.
The witness report states that power/video cables were not shown.

risks.risk: Internal hardware failure or software bricking
risks.proof: A video clip showing the console booting to the dashboard and launching a game.
A screenshot of the 'System Storage' section in the settings menu.
Clear, close-up photos of the front USB ports and the rear HDMI port.
risks.if_unproven: as having damaged ports requiring repair

risks.proof: A video showing a game disc being inserted, recognized by the system, and ejected.
risks.if_unproven: as having a broken disc drive

risks.proof: A photo of both controllers and a video of them being used to navigate the menu.

proof_requests: Photo of the manufacturer's label on the back or bottom showing the specific CUH model number.
Photos of the 2 controllers and 7 games mentioned by the seller.
A video of the console powered on and functioning.
Clear photos of the connection ports on the front and back.
response.reason: The seller's description of the console as 'big' contradicts the witness's observation of a 'slim' design, and the absence of the model label and all claimed accessories makes a reliable valuation impossible.
